cues.en: I wanna share with you a few simulations that model how an epidemic spreads.
cues.zh: 我想和大家分享几个模拟疫情传播的模型。

cues.en: There have recently been a few wonderful interactive articles in this vein, including one in the Washington Post by Harry Stevens, and then another by Kevin Simler over at Melting Asphalt.
cues.zh: 最近有几篇很棒的互动文章，比如《华盛顿邮报》上Harry Stevens的一篇，还有Kevin Simler在Melting Asphalt上的一篇。

cues.en: They are great. You can play with them. They're very informative. I'll, of course, leave links in the description.
cues.zh: 它们很棒，你可以自己动手玩，信息量很大。当然，我会在简介里放上链接。

cues.en: After seeing those, I had a few more questions.
cues.zh: 看完这些之后，我又有了几个问题。

cues.en: Like, if people stay away from each other, I get that that's gonna slow down the spread. But what if despite mostly staying away from each other, people still occasionally go to a central location, like a grocery store or a school?
cues.zh: 比如，如果人们彼此保持距离，我知道这能减缓传播。但如果大家虽然大多保持距离，偶尔还是会去一个中心地点，比如超市或学校，会怎样？

cues.en: Also, what if you're able to identify and isolate the cases? And if you can, what if a few slip through, say, because they don't show symptoms so they aren't tested?
cues.zh: 还有，如果你能识别并隔离病例呢？就算能，如果有几个漏网了呢，比如因为他们没有症状所以没被检测？

cues.en: How does travel between separate communities affect things? And what if people avoid contact with each other for a while, but then they kind of get tired and stop.
cues.zh: 不同社区之间的往来会怎样影响传播？如果人们保持社交距离一段时间，然后有点累了就不再坚持了呢？

cues.en: We'll explore these questions and more, but first, let's walk through how exactly these models will work.
cues.zh: 我们会探讨这些问题以及更多内容，但首先，让我们过一遍这些模型到底是怎么运作的。

cues.en: Each simulation represents what's called an SIR model, meaning the population is broken up into three categories, those who are susceptible to getting the disease, those who are infectious, and then those who have recovered from the infection.
cues.zh: 每个模拟都代表所谓的SIR模型，也就是说人群被分成三类：易感人群、传染期人群，以及已康复人群。

cues.en: So people who are immune don't play into it.
cues.zh: 所以免疫的人不参与其中。

cues.en: The way I've written these, for every unit of time that a susceptible person spends within a certain infection radius of someone with the disease,
cues.zh: 按照我写的规则，易感者在感染半径内与病人共处每单位时间，

cues.en: they'll have some probability of contracting it themselves.
cues.zh: 他们自己就有一定概率被感染。

cues.en: So we're using physical proximity as a stand in for things like shaking hands, touching the same surface, kissing, sneezing on each other, all that good stuff.
cues.zh: 所以我们用物理距离来代表握手、接触同一表面、接吻、互相打喷嚏等等这些行为。

cues.en: Then for each infectious person, after some amount of time, they'll recover and no longer be able to spread the disease.
cues.zh: 然后每个感染者经过一段时间后会康复，不再能传播疾病。

cues.en: Or if they die, they also won't be able to spread it anymore.
cues.zh: 或者如果死亡，也不再能传播。

cues.en: So as a more generic term, sometimes people consider the r in s I r to stand for removed.
cues.zh: 所以作为更通用的说法，有时人们认为SIR中的R代表"移除"。

cues.en: This should go without saying, but let me emphasize it at the start anyway. These are toy models with a tiny population,
cues.zh: 这不用多说，但我还是先强调一下。这些是人口极少的玩具模型，

cues.en: inevitably falling far short of the complexities in real people and larger populations.
cues.zh: 必然远不能反映真实人群和更大群体的复杂性。

cues.en: I am not an epidemiologist,
cues.zh: 我不是流行病学家，

cues.en: so I would be very hesitant to generalize any of the lessons here without deeper consideration.
cues.zh: 所以我会非常谨慎，不加深思不会随便推广这里的任何结论。

cues.en: That said, I think it can be healthy to engage the little scientist inside all of us and take the chance to be experimental
cues.zh: 话虽如此，我认为激发我们每个人内心的小科学家、借机做一些实验

cues.en: and quantitative
cues.zh: 和定量分析

cues.en: even if it's in a necessarily limited fashion,
cues.zh: 即使方式必然有限，

cues.en: especially if the alternative is to dwell on headlines and uncertainty.
cues.zh: 也是有益的，尤其当替代方案是纠结于头条新闻和不确定性时。

cues.en: We'll start things simple and layer on more complexity gradually.
cues.zh: 我们从简单开始，逐步增加复杂度。

cues.en: In these first few runs that you're looking at, everybody is simply meandering around the city in a kind of random walk, and the infection follows the rules that we've laid out.
cues.zh: 在你看的这几轮初始运行中，所有人只是在城市里随机漫步，感染则遵循我们设定的规则。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: it doesn't look great.
cues.zh: 看起来不太妙。

cues.en: After not too long, almost everybody gets infected.
cues.zh: 没过多久，几乎所有人都被感染了。

cues.en: As a sanity check, what would you expect to happen if I double this radius of infection?
cues.zh: 做个合理性检查，如果我把感染半径翻倍，你预期会发生什么？

cues.en: You might think of this as representing more total interactions between people or a more socially engaged society.
cues.zh: 你可以把它理解为代表了人与人之间更多的总互动，或者一个社交更密切的社会。

cues.en: It'll spread more quickly, of course, but how much?
cues.zh: 当然，它会传播得更快，但快多少呢？

cues.en: It's actually very drastic.
cues.zh: 实际上非常剧烈。

cues.en: Within a short time span, the majority of our little population is infected simultaneously.
cues.zh: 在很短的时间内，我们这个小群体中的大多数人同时被感染。

cues.en: As another sanity check, what would you expect if we go back to the original infection radius and then we cut the probability of infection in half?
cues.zh: 再做一次合理性检查，如果我们回到原来的感染半径，然后把感染概率减半，你预期会怎样？

cues.en: Remember, the way this is running, for each day that a susceptible person is within that radius of an infectious person, they have some probability of becoming infected.
cues.zh: 记住，按这个运行方式，对于易感者处于感染者该半径内的每一天，他们都有一定的概率被感染。

cues.en: By default, I've set it to twenty percent, but this is the number that we're now gonna cut in half.
cues.zh: 默认我设成了百分之二十，而这就是我们现在要减半的数字。

cues.en: You might think of this as better handwashing,
cues.zh: 你可以把它理解为更好的洗手，

cues.en: better cough protection, and less face touching.
cues.zh: 更好的咳嗽防护，以及更少触摸面部。

cues.en: As you might expect, it spreads out the curve.
cues.zh: 如你所料，它把曲线拉平了。

cues.en: In fact, it does this by quite a lot, which really illustrates how changes to hygiene have very large effects on the rate of spreading.
cues.zh: 事实上，拉平的程度相当大，这很好地说明了卫生习惯的改变对传播速度有非常大的影响。

cues.en: The first of several key takeaways here that I'd like you to tuck away in your mind is just how sensitive this growth can be to each parameter in our control.
cues.zh: 首先，我要请你记住的几个关键要点之一是，这种增长对每个我们可控的参数有多敏感。

cues.en: It's not that hard to imagine changing your daily habits in a way that multiplies the number of people you interact with or that cuts your probability of catching an infection in half.
cues.zh: 不难想象，改变日常习惯，让你接触的人数成倍增加，或者把感染概率减半。

cues.en: But the implications for the pace of the spread are huge.
cues.zh: 但这对传播速度的影响是巨大的。

cues.en: The goal is probably to reduce the total number of people who die, which is gonna be some proportion of this removed category in the end.
cues.zh: 目标大概是减少总死亡人数，而这最终会是移除类别中的一定比例。

cues.en: That proportion is not a constant, though. If you get to a point where the peak of the infection curve is too high, meaning there's a time when many people are all sick at once, that's the point when available health care resources are overwhelmed, which for a bad disease will increase the mortality rate.
cues.zh: 不过这个比例不是固定的。如果感染曲线的峰值太高，意味着有一段时间很多人同时生病，那时可用的医疗资源就会被压垮，对于严重的疾病，这会提高死亡率。

cues.en: Now I don't know where you're from, but in most towns, people don't actually spend their days drunkenly wandering around the city like this. Often, there's a common destination, like a central market or a school.
cues.zh: 我不知道你来自哪里，但在大多数城镇，人们不会整天醉醺醺地在城里这样闲逛。通常，有一个共同的目的地，比如中央市场或学校。

cues.en: In our model, if we introduce some central spot like this that people regularly visit and then return from, it's...
cues.zh: 在我们的模型中，如果我们引入这样一个人们经常去又返回的中央地点，那就……

cues.en: Well, just look.
cues.zh: 嗯，看看就知道了。

cues.en: One of the main things I was curious about is how to mitigate this effect, and that's something we'll examine in just a bit.
cues.zh: 我好奇的主要事情之一是如何减轻这种效应，我们稍后会探讨。

cues.en: Another feature that we could include is to have a few separate communities with transit between them. Every day, each person will have some probability of traveling to the center of another community and then going about their usual routine from there.
cues.zh: 我们能加入的另一个功能是，设置几个独立的社区，彼此之间有往来。每天，每个人都会有一定概率前往另一个社区的中心，再从那里开始日常活动。

cues.en: All of that is our basic setup. So now the question is what actions help to stop this spread?
cues.zh: 以上就是我们的基础设定。那么现在的问题是，哪些措施有助于阻止这种传播？

cues.en: What is by far most effective is to identify and isolate whoever is infectious,
cues.zh: 目前最有效的是识别并隔离任何有传染性的人，

cues.en: for example, with good testing and quick responsiveness.
cues.zh: 比如，通过良好的检测和快速的响应。

cues.en: In our simulations, once we hit some critical threshold of cases, we're gonna start sending people to a separate location
cues.zh: 在我们的模拟中，一旦病例达到某个临界阈值，我们就会开始把感染者送到一个单独的地点，

cues.en: one day after they have the infection.
cues.zh: 在他们感染后的一天。

cues.en: This is, of course, a stand in for whatever isolation would look like in the real world. It doesn't have to literally be transporting all the sick people into one sad box.
cues.zh: 当然，这只是现实世界中隔离措施的一种替代表现。并不一定真的要字面意义上把所有病人都塞进一个可怜的小盒子里。

cues.en: Unsurprisingly,
cues.zh: 不出所料，

cues.en: this totally halts the epidemic in its tracks.
cues.zh: 这完全阻止了疫情的蔓延。

cues.en: But what if when you're infected, you have a twenty percent chance of not getting quarantined?
cues.zh: 但如果你被感染时，有百分之二十的概率不会被隔离呢？

cues.en: Say, because you show no symptoms so you don't get tested, and you go about your day as usual.
cues.zh: 比如说，因为你没有症状所以没去做检测，然后照常过你的日子。

cues.en: We're gonna illustrate these people that have no symptoms using yellow circles instead of red.
cues.zh: 我们用黄色圆圈而不是红色来表示这些没有症状的人。

cues.en: Obviously, this will have a result somewhere between a total quarantine and doing nothing.
cues.zh: 显然，结果会介于完全隔离和什么都不做之间。

cues.en: But where on the spectrum would you predict it'll be?
cues.zh: 但你预测它会落在光谱的哪个位置？

cues.en: The peak number of simultaneous cases is only a little bit higher, but there is a very long tail as it takes a much longer time to stamp out, resulting in about twice as many total cases.
cues.zh: 同时感染人数的峰值只是略高一点，但有一个很长的尾巴，因为需要长得多的时间才能彻底消灭，导致总病例数大约翻倍。

cues.en: This gets more interesting when we do it in a setting with many communities and transit between them. Again, totally effective tracking in isolation stops the epidemic very quickly.
cues.zh: 在有很多社区且彼此之间有往来的环境中，这就变得更有意思了。再次强调，完全有效的隔离追踪能很快阻止流行病。

cues.en: But what would you predict is gonna happen if now twenty percent of the infectious cases slip through that process?
cues.zh: 但如果现在有20%的感染病例漏过了这个流程，你预测会发生什么？

cues.en: Again, I've set things to wait until a certain critical threshold of cases is hit before our little dot society kicks into gear and takes action. As a side note, it's a little interesting that even when all the parameters are the same, some runs take three times longer to reach this point than others. Before the law of large numbers kicks in, that pace of growth can have as much to do with the roll of the dice as it does with anything intrinsic to the disease itself.
cues.zh: 同样，我设定要等到病例达到某个临界阈值，我们这个小点社会才会启动并采取行动。顺便说一句，有意思的是，即使所有参数都相同，有些运行达到这个点所需的时间是其他的三倍。在大数定律起作用之前，这种增长速度可能更多取决于掷骰子的运气，而不是疾病本身的内在特性。

cues.en: This leaky quarantining effort definitely flattens out the curve, but it is a much thicker tail, and it takes a much longer time to track down all the cases with over half the population getting infected this time.
cues.zh: 这种有漏洞的隔离措施确实让曲线变平了，但尾部厚得多，追踪所有病例所需的时间也长得多，这次超过一半的人口被感染。

cues.en: Now what would you predict if it was only fifty percent of the infectious cases that were isolated like this?
cues.zh: 那么，如果只有50%的感染病例被这样隔离，你预测会怎样？

cues.en: If half the infectious people are getting quarantined,
cues.zh: 如果一半的感染者被隔离，

cues.en: it doesn't mean that half the total population will end up with the disease.
cues.zh: 并不意味着总人口的一半最终会得病。

cues.en: Because there are so many agents still out there spreading it, we end up with a situation that's only barely better than if nothing had been done at all.
cues.zh: 因为还有太多代理在外面传播，我们最终的情况只比什么都没做稍微好一点点。

cues.en: A second key takeaway here is that changes in how many people slip through the tests can cause disproportionately
cues.zh: 第二个关键点是，通过检测的人数变化，会造成感染总人数不成比例的大幅变化。

cues.en: large changes to the total number of people infected.
cues.zh: 感染总人数会出现不成比例的大幅变化。

cues.en: If we look back to the fact that quickly containing cases so early is so effective,
cues.zh: 如果我们回顾一下，早期快速控制病例是如此有效，

cues.en: it actually has an interesting corollary, which is that the most lethal diseases are, in some sense, less dangerous globally.
cues.zh: 这其实有个有趣的推论：最致命的疾病，从某种意义上说，在全球范围内反而没那么危险。

cues.en: Remember that the rule of this quarantine simulation is to send infectious people to a separate spot one day after they've been infected.
cues.zh: 记住，这个隔离模拟的规则是，在感染者被感染一天后，将其送到单独的地点。

cues.en: But if the disease kills its host after one day, the model looks identical.
cues.zh: 但如果这种疾病在一天后就杀死宿主，模型看起来是一样的。

cues.en: It just has a much darker interpretation.
cues.zh: 只是解读起来要黑暗得多。

cues.en: It is terrible for those who get it, but it doesn't spread.
cues.zh: 对感染者来说很可怕，但它不会传播。

cues.en: It also means that the most dangerous viruses are the ones that kill some part of the population
cues.zh: 这也意味着，最危险的病毒是那些杀死部分人群

cues.en: while laying unnoticed and spreadable among others. Or worse yet, if they remain unnoticed and spreadable in everyone before eventually becoming lethal.
cues.zh: 同时在其他人中悄无声息地传播的病毒。更糟的是，如果它们在最终变得致命之前，在所有人中都悄无声息地传播。

cues.en: One of the reasons that the SARS outbreak in 2002 was so well contained is that just about everybody in this infectious population
cues.zh: 2002年SARS疫情之所以能被很好地控制，原因之一是，在这个感染人群中，几乎每个人

cues.en: was showing symptoms, so they were much easier to identify and isolate.
cues.zh: 都出现了症状，因此更容易识别和隔离。

cues.en: A more optimistic corollary of these quarantine simulations is how useful early treatment can be. If there exists an antiviral therapeutic that can move people out of this infectious category quickly, it has the same effect on the model as isolating those cases.
cues.zh: 这些隔离模拟的一个更乐观的推论是，早期治疗多么有用。如果存在一种抗病毒疗法，能迅速让人脱离感染类别，它对模型的效果与隔离这些病例相同。

cues.en: But let's say you don't have widespread testing or antiviral therapeutics.
cues.zh: 但假设你没有大范围检测或抗病毒疗法。

cues.en: Well, let's introduce a new parameter here, which is how much people try to avoid each other. Let's call it the social distance factor.
cues.zh: 那么，我们在这里引入一个新参数，也就是人们尝试互相回避的程度。我们把它称为社交距离因子。

cues.en: In these animations,
cues.zh: 在这些动画里，

cues.en: I'll apply it as a repulsive force between people and have them glow yellow when they feel just a little too close to their neighbor.
cues.zh: 我会把它作为人与人之间的排斥力，并让它们觉得离邻居稍微太近时发黄光。

cues.en: This has the sad but kind of cute effect that when our little agents are social distancing, they often end up trembling near the edge of their box.
cues.zh: 这会产生一种悲伤但有点可爱的效果：当我们的这些小代理保持社交距离时，它们常常会在自己的方框边缘附近发抖。

cues.en: No isolation is perfect, though, so every now and then, even those repulsed by each other will kind of jiggle close enough to get infected.
cues.zh: 不过没有哪种隔离是完美的，所以偶尔即使是互相排斥的个体，也会晃动着靠近到足以被感染。

cues.en: The point is that those interactions are much rarer.
cues.zh: 关键是这些接触要少得多。

cues.en: Let's take a look at four separate runs here. In each one of them, after we hit fifty cases, I'll turn on social distancing.
cues.zh: 我们来看看这里的四次独立运行。每一次，在病例达到五十例后，我都会开启社交距离。

cues.en: But in the top left, we'll turn it on for everybody.
cues.zh: 但在左上角，我们会为所有人开启。

cues.en: In the top right, we'll turn it on for ninety percent of the population.
cues.zh: 在右上角，我们会为百分之九十的人口开启。

cues.en: In the bottom left, for seventy percent of the population,
cues.zh: 在左下角，对百分之七十的人口开启，

cues.en: and in the bottom right, for only half the population.
cues.zh: 而右下角，只对一半人口开启。

cues.en: What would you predict is gonna happen?
cues.zh: 你预测会发生什么？

cues.en: As you might expect, when one hundred percent of people avoid each other, the disease quickly goes away entirely.
cues.zh: 正如你可能预料的那样，当百分之百的人互相回避时，疾病会很快完全消失。

cues.en: And in all four cases, the presence of some kind of widespread social distancing definitely flattens out the curve.
cues.zh: 而且在所有四种情况中，存在某种大范围社交距离，确实能让曲线变平。

cues.en: However, in terms of the ultimate number of cases, the run with seventy percent and even the one with ninety percent end up with a little less than half the population ultimately getting infected,
cues.zh: 不过，就最终的感染人数而言，70% 的那组甚至 90% 的那组，最终也只有不到一半的人口被感染，

cues.en: which is only a tiny bit better than the one with fifty percent.
cues.zh: 只比 50% 的那组好一点点。

cues.en: That case with ninety percent of people repelling each other certainly takes longer to get there, but evidently, a mere ten percent of the population cheating
cues.zh: 90% 的人互相保持距离的那组当然花了更长时间才达到这个结果，但显然，仅仅 10% 的人“作弊”

cues.en: adds enough instability to our system to keep the fire slowly burning for a long time.
cues.zh: 就给系统带来了足够的不稳定性，让火苗能慢慢地烧上很长时间。

cues.en: Again, I'll emphasize that these are toy models, and I leave it to the intelligence of the viewer to judge if the behavior of these little dots accurately reflects what social distancing would mean for you and your life.
cues.zh: 再强调一下，这些都是玩具模型，至于这些小圆点的行为是否能准确反映保持社交距离对你和你的生活意味着什么，就留给观众自行判断了。

cues.en: Someone fully sequestered in their home is not necessarily affected by the random jigglings of their neighbor. But then again, few of us genuinely live independently from everyone else.
cues.zh: 完全居家隔离的人未必会受到邻居随机活动的影响。但话说回来，我们当中很少有人真正与他人完全隔绝地生活。

cues.en: Insofar as these models aren't outlandish,
cues.zh: 如果这些模型还算靠谱的话，

cues.en: the third key takeaway is that social distancing absolutely works to flatten the curve, but even small imperfections prolong the spread for a while.
cues.zh: 第三个关键结论就是：保持社交距离确实能有效地拉平曲线，但哪怕是很小的不完美也会让疫情蔓延延长一段时间。

cues.en: Now let's look at that setup with 12 communities and travel between them. By default, I have set so that every day, each agent has a 2% chance of traveling to the center of a different community.
cues.zh: 现在我们来看那个有 12 个社区、社区之间存在往来.travel 的设定。默认情况下，我设置了每天每个个体有 2% 的概率旅行到另一个社区的中心。

cues.en: Now let's try a run where once we hit a 100 cases, we cut down that travel rate by a factor of four to only half a percent. What would you predict is gonna happen?
cues.zh: 现在我们来试一次：一旦达到 100 个病例，我们就把出行率削减到四分之一，也就是只有 0.5%。你猜会发生什么？

cues.en: The honest answer is that it depends. In some runs, it doesn't make any difference, and the majority of every community gets it.
cues.zh: 诚实的答案是：视情况而定。在某些运行中，它没有任何区别，每个社区中的大多数人都被感染了。

cues.en: Other times, there are a couple communities that end up unscathed.
cues.zh: 其他时候，有几个社区最终毫发无损。

cues.en: In general, the earlier you turn on this effect, the more effective it is. But the takeaway here is that reducing contact between communities
cues.zh: 一般来说，越早开启这个效果，它就越有效。但这里的要点是，减少社区之间的接触

cues.en: really has only a limited effect once those communities already have it. And as solutions go, it's certainly not robust on its own.
cues.zh: 一旦这些社区已经感染，效果其实非常有限。而且作为解决方案，它本身显然不够稳健。

cues.en: As a side note, when we run these simulations with larger cities, which has the effect that city centers act like concentrated urban hubs, you can see how as soon as the infection hits one of these urban centers, it very quickly hits all of them.
cues.zh: 顺便说一句，当我们用更大的城市运行这些模拟时，城市中心就像集中的城市枢纽，你可以看到一旦感染袭击了其中一个城市中心，它就会非常迅速地袭击所有城市中心。

cues.en: And after that, it slowly spreads to the edges of each community.
cues.zh: 之后，它会缓慢地蔓延到每个社区的边缘。

cues.en: Let's take a moment to talk about how to quantify this spread.
cues.zh: 让我们花点时间谈谈如何量化这种传播。

cues.en: Consider one person with the disease and then count how many people they infect while they have it.
cues.zh: 考虑一个患病的人，然后统计他们在患病期间感染了多少人。

cues.en: The average for this count across everybody who's been sick is known as the effective reproductive number or r.
cues.zh: 对每个患过病的人取这个计数的平均值，被称为有效再生数或 r。

cues.en: A more commonly discussed number is r naught, which is the value of r in a fully susceptible population,
cues.zh: 一个更常讨论的数字是 r naught，即 r 在完全易感人群中的值，

cues.en: like at the very beginning. This is known as the basic reproductive number.
cues.zh: 比如在最开始的时候。这被称为基本再生数。

cues.en: You may have noticed I have this little label on our simulations,
cues.zh: 你可能注意到我在模拟上有一个小标签，

cues.en: and the way that it's being calculated is to look at each individual who's currently infectious, count how many people they've infected so far, estimate how many they're going to infect in total based on the duration of the illness,
cues.zh: 它的计算方式是，查看每个当前具有传染性的个体，统计他们到目前为止感染了多少人，根据疾病持续时间估算他们总共会感染多少人，

cues.en: and then average those numbers.
cues.zh: 然后对这些数字取平均值。

cues.en: For example, in our first default simulation with no added spices, r is around 2.2 at the highest part of the growth phase before falling down as the population becomes saturated.
cues.zh: 比如，在我们最初没有添加任何变量的默认模拟中，r在增长阶段的最高点大约是2.2，随后随着种群饱和而下降。

cues.en: By contrast, when we doubled the infection radius, r was as high as eight.
cues.zh: 相比之下，当我们将感染半径加倍时，r高达8。

cues.en: This factor has a huge effect on the growth rate.
cues.zh: 这个因素对增长率有巨大影响。

cues.en: It should kind of make sense that it jumped up as high as eight, though. When you double that radius, there's about four times as many people inside it to infect.
cues.zh: 不过，它跳到高达8也说得通。当半径加倍时，半径内可感染的人数大约变成四倍。

cues.en: When we chopped the infection rate in half, it hovered around the one point three to one point seven range.
cues.zh: 当我们将感染率减半时，r在1.3到1.7之间徘徊。

cues.en: While r is greater than one, the infection is growing exponentially,
cues.zh: 当r大于1时，感染呈指数增长，

cues.en: and it's at that point that it's known as an epidemic.
cues.zh: 此时它被称为流行病。

cues.en: When it holds steady around one, that's when a disease is called endemic.
cues.zh: 当r稳定在1左右时，疾病被称为地方性流行。

cues.en: And less than one means that it's on the decline.
cues.zh: 小于1则意味着它在下降。

cues.en: For comparison, r naught for COVID nineteen is estimated to be a little above two,
cues.zh: 作为对比，COVID-19的R0估计略高于2，

cues.en: which is also around what the mean estimate for r naught was during the nineteen eighteen Spanish flu pandemic.
cues.zh: 这也大致是1918年西班牙流感大流行期间R0平均估计值的水平。

cues.en: The seasonal flu by comparison is much lower, around 1.3.
cues.zh: 相比之下，季节性流感要低得多，约为1.3。

cues.en: In the travel case, as soon as we turn on social distancing and shut down travel,
cues.zh: 在旅行场景中，一旦我们开启社交距离并关闭旅行，

cues.en: you can see r quickly dropped down from two. There's a little bit of a lag between the change we make to the model and the value of this number since it's calculated based on current infectious cases, which might have existed prior to the method being put in place.
cues.zh: 你可以看到r迅速从2下降。我们修改模型与该数值变化之间存在一点滞后，因为它是基于当前感染病例计算的，而这些病例可能在该措施实施之前就已存在。

cues.en: Like I said at the start, one of the things I was most curious about is the effect of some kind of shared central location, like a market or a school.
cues.zh: 就像我一开始说的，我最想知道的事情之一，就是某种共享的中心场所的影响，比如市场或学校。

cues.en: When I introduce such a destination for our little dots, r naught jumps as high as 5.8.
cues.zh: 当我为这些小点引入这样一个目的地时，r naught 会跃升到高达 5.8。

cues.en: This might be a little unfair since it puts everyone right in the same spot. And given that we're using physical proximity as a stand in for things like shaking hands or kissing,
cues.zh: 这可能有点不太公平，因为这把所有人都放到了同一个地方。考虑到我们是把物理上的接近当作握手或接吻等行为的替代，

cues.en: we should maybe acknowledge that people going to the same school or grocery store are not as likely to spread an infection as, say, close friends or people living in the same house.
cues.zh: 我们也许应该承认，去同一所学校或同一家杂货店的人，传播感染的几率并不像密友或住在同一屋檐下的人那么高。

cues.en: To account for this, let's conservatively cut the probability of infection per day in half.
cues.zh: 为了考虑这一点，我们保守地把每天的感染概率减半。

cues.en: This does indeed cut r naught in half, but the effect of a central market remains dramatic.
cues.zh: 这确实把 r naught 减半了，但中心市场的影响依然很显著。

cues.en: Now let's try a run where after some threshold is hit, we turn on social distancing,
cues.zh: 现在让我们试一次运行，在达到某个阈值后，我们开启社交距离措施，

cues.en: but people still go to that central location the way they did before.
cues.zh: 但人们仍然像以前一样去那个中心场所。

cues.en: You may notice that some of our little dots seem to have escaped their little cage,
cues.zh: 你可能注意到，我们的一些小点似乎逃出了它们的小笼子，

cues.en: which was not supposed to happen,
cues.zh: 这本不该发生，

cues.en: but I am going to make the conscious choice not to fix that. It's like they all looked at the chaos inside and just went, nope. I'm out. I don't want any part of that. Living in the Bay Area during a shelter in place order, I can confirm that this is how some people react.
cues.zh: 但我会有意选择不去修复它。就像它们都看了看里面的混乱，然后直接说，不了。我退出。我不想掺和这个。在居家隔离令期间住在湾区，我可以确认，有些人就是这么反应的。

cues.en: Wandering dots aside, though, let me show you how this graph compares to the control case where we did nothing and how it compares to what would have happened if in addition to repelling from each other, all of the dots also stopped going to that central location.
cues.zh: 抛开那些游走的点不谈，让我展示一下这张图与对照组（我们什么都没做）的对比，以及如果除了相互排斥之外，所有点也停止前往那个中心位置会发生什么。

cues.en: The peak of the infection curve is a little bit lower than the control, but in terms of the total number of cases, keeping that central location active
cues.zh: 感染曲线的峰值比对照组略低一些，但就总病例数而言，保持那个中心位置活跃

cues.en: really defeats the effects of otherwise social distancing.
cues.zh: 确实抵消了社交距离的效果。

cues.en: Now let me ask you to make a prediction. What do you think will be more effective if on top of that social distancing effect, we decrease the frequency with which people go to that central spot, maybe by a factor of five,
cues.zh: 现在让我请大家做一个预测。你们觉得，在社交距离效应的基础上，如果我们把人们前往那个中心地点的频率降低，比如降低到五分之一，

cues.en: or if we chop the probability of infection down by another factor of two, For example, meaning people are super extra cautious about washing their hands and not touching their face.
cues.zh: 或者把感染概率再降低一半，比如人们格外注意洗手、不碰脸，哪个会更有效？

cues.en: The simulation on the left requires our dots to very heavily alter their daily routines,
cues.zh: 左边的模拟要求我们的点大幅改变日常习惯，

cues.en: whereas on the right, our dots can mostly continue their usual habits, but they're just much more conscious of hygiene.
cues.zh: 而右边，我们的点基本可以继续日常习惯，只是对卫生更加注意。

cues.en: They're actually nearly identical,
cues.zh: 它们实际上几乎完全相同，

cues.en: which surprised me given that one of them is a fivefold decrease and the other is twofold.
cues.zh: 这让我很惊讶，因为一个是降低五倍，另一个是降低两倍。

cues.en: I guess it goes to show that effective hygiene,
cues.zh: 我想这说明有效的卫生习惯，

cues.en: which is maybe easier said than done, really goes a long way.
cues.zh: 说起来容易做起来难，但确实大有裨益。

cues.en: Of course, it doesn't have to be an either or. Our goal with these experiments is to look at the effects of one change at a time.
cues.zh: 当然，这不一定是二选一。我们做这些实验的目标，是每次只观察一个变化带来的影响。

cues.en: If you're curious, here's what it looks like when we apply social distancing, we restrict the rate that people go to the central location, and we also lower the infection rate all at once.
cues.zh: 如果你好奇的话，当我们同时采取社交距离、限制人们前往中心地点的频率，并降低感染率时，情况是这样的。

cues.en: This combination is indeed very effective.
cues.zh: 这种组合确实非常有效。

cues.en: But I wanna emphasize again how the most desirable case is when you can consistently identify and isolate cases.
cues.zh: 但我想再次强调，最理想的情况是你能持续地识别并隔离病例。

cues.en: Even in this central market simulation,
cues.zh: 即使在这个中心市场模拟中，

cues.en: which left unchecked gives a huge conflagration,
cues.zh: 不加控制会引发大规模爆发，

cues.en: being able to do this effectively still halts the epidemic.
cues.zh: 能有效做到这一点仍然可以阻止流行病。

cues.en: And our little dots don't even have to be repelled by each other or stop their trips to the central spot.
cues.zh: 而且我们的小圆点甚至不需要互相排斥，也不需要停止前往中心地点。

cues.en: In real epidemiology,
cues.zh: 顺便说一句，在真实的流行病学中，

cues.en: by the way, it gets way more sophisticated than this with tactics like contact tracing,
cues.zh: 情况要比这复杂得多，会用到接触者追踪等策略，

cues.en: where you not only identify and isolate known cases, but you do the same for everyone who's been in contact with those cases.
cues.zh: 你不仅要识别并隔离已知病例，还要对与这些病例有过接触的所有人做同样的事。

cues.en: Given the time that I'm posting this, I imagine there's some expectation for it to be a PSA on social distancing.
cues.zh: 考虑到我发布这个视频的时间，我想有人会期待它成为关于社交距离的公益宣传。

cues.en: But to be honest, that's not really my own main takeaway.
cues.zh: 但说实话，那并不是我自己最主要的收获。

cues.en: To be clear, when it's needed, like it is now, social distancing absolutely saves lives. And as we saw earlier, when people cheat or when they continue to regularly meet at a central spot, it has a disproportionate effect on the long term number of cases.
cues.zh: 明确地说，在需要的时候，就像现在这样，社交距离绝对能拯救生命。而且正如我们之前看到的，当人们违规或者继续定期在中心地点聚集时，会对长期病例数量产生不成比例的影响。

cues.en: The uncomfortable truth, though, is that while the disease still exists, as soon as people let up and they go back to their normal lives, if nothing is in place to contain the cases, few though they might be, you'll just get a second wave.
cues.zh: 令人不安的事实是，尽管疾病依然存在，一旦人们松懈下来、回归正常生活，如果没有控制病例的措施，哪怕病例很少，也会迎来第二波疫情。

cues.en: After making all of these, what I came away with more than anything else was a deeper appreciation for disease control done right, for the inordinate value of early widespread testing and the ability to isolate cases,
cues.zh: 做完这一切后，我最大的收获是对正确开展疾病控制有了更深的认识，对早期广泛检测和隔离病例能力的巨大价值有了更深的体会，

cues.en: for therapeutics that treat these cases, and most importantly,
cues.zh: 对治疗这些病例的方法，最重要的是，

cues.en: for how easy it is to underestimate all that value when times are good.
cues.zh: 对在顺境时多么容易低估这一切价值有了更深的体会。

cues.en: I'm writing this during a pandemic when some viewers may be able to identify a little too well with the trembling dots retreating to the edge of their box.
cues.zh: 我写这篇文章时正值一场大流行病期间，有些观众可能对那个颤抖的小点退缩到方框边缘的画面感同身受，甚至有些过于真切。

cues.en: But in the future, many people will be watching this during a pandemic that never was,
cues.zh: 但未来，很多人会在看这段内容时，正值一场从未发生的大流行病，

cues.en: a time when a novel pathogen that could have spread widely if left unchecked was instead swiftly found and contained.
cues.zh: 那时，一种本可广泛传播的新病原体若放任不管，却被迅速发现并控制住了。

cues.en: Those would be pandemics never make it into the history books, which is maybe why we don't value the heroes behind them the way that we should.
cues.zh: 那些大流行病从未载入史册，这也许正是我们没有恰如其分地珍视背后英雄的原因。

cues.en: Living in a world with widespread travel and vibrant urban centers does make fighting the spread of a disease an uphill battle. That's absolutely true.
cues.zh: 生活在一个旅行普及、城市中心充满活力的世界里，抗击疾病传播确实是一场硬仗。这绝对是真的。

cues.en: But that same level of connectedness means that ideas spread more quickly than ever, ideas that can lead to systems and technologies that nip these outbreaks in the bud. It won't happen on its own, and it's clear that we sometimes make mistakes, but I'm fundamentally optimistic about our ability to learn from those mistakes.
cues.zh: 但同样的互联程度意味着思想传播比以往任何时候都快，这些思想能催生将疫情扼杀在萌芽状态的系统和技术。这不会自动发生，我们也显然有时会犯错，但我对我们从错误中学习的能力 fundamentally 持乐观态度。

cues.en: As you might imagine, these videos require a lot of hours of effort. I don't do any ad reads at the end, and YouTube content related to the current pandemic seems to be systematically demonetized.
cues.zh: 可以想象，这些视频需要投入大量时间精力。我从不做广告口播，而且YouTube上与当前疫情相关的内容似乎被系统性地取消了收益。

cues.en: So I just wanna take this chance to say a particularly warm thank you to those who support them directly on Patreon.
cues.zh: 所以我想借此机会，特别诚挚地感谢那些直接在Patreon上支持我的人。

cues.en: It really does make a difference.
cues.zh: 这确实意义重大。
